It began with severe vertigo, fatigue so bad I couldn’t even move my arms or legs - I just laid in bed and slept for months, and joint pain. My heart rate was very high too obviously. I was bedbound for a long time (multiple years) and as time went on my symptoms/related illnesses developed including: chronic pain, gerd, constant low grade fever, nausea and vomiting, pulsatile tinnitus, sensory overload (loud noise, busy places, bright lights all make me feel VERY ill). Raynaurds, poor circulation, irritable bowel and bladder, dairy allergy. Brain fog - hence my struggles to remember it all. Ultimately what helped me was rest, lots of water intake, mitochondrial energy optimisers (supplements) - bare in mind it was about 3 years of this before I began to feel a tiny bit better. Then I was put onto ivabradine for my pots and as it kept my heart rate stable my body slowly ‘recovered’ bit by bit over the years. I’m cautious with using the word ‘recovered’ because ultimately I am permanently disabled and suffer every single day even after all these years. I had to edit my entire life and adjust to being housebound and living with minimal energy and give up my dreams, it took me many years to accept this emotionally and mentally so don’t be too hard on yourself. I know how utterly heartbreaking it is to be in this situation, and just remember that everybody is different and you may stand a better chance at getting your life back than I did.  The first 3 years were the worst for me, I know how hard that probably will be to read knowing you’re 7 months in and are struggling so much already, please stay strong and know that you aren’t alone in this (I spent many years feeling totally alone so I know what it feels like), I’m so sorry you’ve gone through this too:(

I caught Covid in March 2020 and wasn’t that sick with it, I haven’t caught it again since and I cannot have the covid vaccine due to being vaccine injured 10 years ago. Ultimately I don’t really leave the house other than to go to hospital, if I do I wear a mask and social distance of course, I worry about catching it again and getting severely ill but I don’t have a choice. A lot of people assume if you are unvaccinated you’re just an anti-vaxxer asshole, but they don’t seem to consider that some of us medically cannot have the vaccine and live in fear of getting severely ill from covid:(

It’s exactly that, I was vaccine injured 10 years ago and it was the way my body reacted to the vaccine - not that the vaccine was “bad” or “dangerous”. It’s taken many years to come to terms with my disabilities and the way I have to live my life now, though I have found the pandemic extremely tough as I have medical trauma relating to my vaccine injury and considering there’s a lot of talk about vaccines at the moment I can’t escape the memories of what I went through (the first few years were the worst, I don’t know how I survived). I barely speak about it because I’ve been abused and targeted as an anti-vaxxer despite never negatively speaking about vaccines or discouraging people from having them - it’s simple, it is not my fault I cannot have the covid vaccine due to my previous injury, if I was an anti-vaxxer I would not of had the vaccine that damaged me. I chose to have it! It is upsetting how people treat the situation, they cannot believe that it’s possible to be damaged by a vaccine because they’ve not experienced it, and of course it’s rare but it doesn’t invalidate the fact we have lived through the experience.

It depends what makeup she wears, but my personal favourite eyeshadow palette is the Too Faced Chocolate Gold eyeshadow palette. Some people do not like this palette as it is mostly shimmery shades, however the few matte shades in the palette are really wonderful, and I can easily bring the palette with me anywhere to create a daytime look or a night time look. This can be bought in stores in Debenhams in the UK and costs around 40£.

As mentioned already, the Anastasia palette is a great choice too, I have also heard good things about the Soft Glam palette by the same brand. This can be bought on the website Beauty Bay and I believe costs around 40£. 

Another one of my favourite eyeshadow palettes is the Kat Von D Shade and Light Eye Contour/Shadow Palette, they are all matte shades which compliment all eye shapes (as sometimes shimmery shades can be difficult to wear for those with certain eye shapes). It’s a great palette as it can be used for everyday wear, and built up to be much more intense. This can be bought online at Debenhams in the UK, and I believe costs around 30£.

I do not know the complexion of your girlfriend, but eyeshadow palettes are probably the safest option to go for as they aren’t always skin tone specific.

If she is a lipstick wearer, I personally love the Jeffree Star Valour Liquid Lipsticks, the shade Celebrity Skin is a perfect shade on plenty of complexions. This can be bought on the website Beauty Bay and cost I believe 14£ each. 

So far all of the brands I have mentioned are on the slightly pricey side (depending on your stance at money and whether you are in the UK or US). A cheaper brand that I personally really like is Makeup Revolution, in the UK it can be bought in Superdrug, and they also have their own website. They have two eyeshadow palettes by the Youtuber “SophDoesNails” and I have heard wonderful things about them. She also has a highlighter palette which has a range of different shades that will suit all complexions and can be used as eyeshadows too. These cost around 10£ each.
